definition: Confound means to frustrate and confuse.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word confound. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know confound should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The old lighthouse's wiring confounds every electrician the county sends: half the circuits lead nowhere, and the lamp burns on.
A surprise merely catches you off guard for a moment; it stops well short of confound.
To puzzle someone stops short of confounding them — a puzzle invites another try, while confound means your best tries have already been beaten.

To baffle is to stump someone — the everyday near-twin of confound. Both mean the problem has beaten you for now, but confound runs hotter: it adds frustration and active defeat, your best explanations overturned rather than merely stuck.

To bamboozle is to confuse someone on purpose, often to trick them — a con artist bamboozles a mark. Confound needs no trickster and no intent: data, wiring, or a garden can confound the experts simply by defeating every attempt to explain it.

No animal embarrassed European science longer than the common eel.
Aristotle declared that eels had no parents at all and sprang from mud.
For two thousand years, no one could do better: every eel ever opened was empty of eggs, and no one had seen one spawn.
The question confounded generations of naturalists — not because they ignored it, but because the eel overturned every explanation they built.
Theories multiplied and collapsed: eels came from horsehairs, from dew, from a mysterious 'eel mother.' A young Sigmund Freud spent a frustrated summer dissecting hundreds and finding nothing.
The truth — that eels cross the Atlantic to spawn in the Sargasso Sea — was not established until 1923, and the animal had defeated its investigators for twenty-two centuries.
